transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*storms into the rehearsal hall, face flushed with frustration*

Salieri! I've been away for two weeks on the Emperor's business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don't know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

*slams music portfolio down on the nearby table*

What in God's name happened here? I leave Vienna for a fortnight and return to find absolute chaos! Do you have ANY explanation for this disaster?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My dear colleague, it is indeed regrettable to see you in such distress. I assure you, I have done my utmost to maintain order in your absence. However, it appears that unforeseen circumstances have led to this unfortunate situation.

First and foremost, I must address the issue of the singers' lack of preparation. I understand the importance of their readiness for the upcoming performance, and I will personally ensure that they are brought up to speed promptly.

As for the missing second violin parts, I can only offer my sincerest apologies. It seems there was a misunderstanding in the distribution of responsibilities, and I take full responsibility for this oversight. I will make it my priority to have those parts copied and distributed without delay.

Regarding the rewriting of your stage directions without consultation, I share your dismay. It is essential for all aspects of the production to be in harmony, and I regret any disruption caused by this alteration. Rest assured, I will work with you to rectify this situation and ensure that your artistic vision is preserved.

I understand the gravity of the situation with the premiere drawing near, and I am committed to working together with you to bring order back to our preparations. Let us put our minds and talents together to overcome these challenges and present a performance that will do justice to the music and the opera.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*waves hand dismissively, pacing back and forth*

Unforeseen circumstances? UNFORESEEN? Salieri, managing a rehearsal schedule is not some act of divine providence subject to the whims of fate! It is ORGANIZATION! It is DISCIPLINE! Things I believed you possessed in abundance!

*turns to face him directly, voice sharp*

And "misunderstanding in the distribution of responsibilities"? There WAS no distribution! YOU were responsible for EVERYTHING while I was gone! That was our agreement! I trusted you completely, and now you stand there offering me these... these PLATITUDES about working together and preserving artistic vision!

*picks up a sheet of music from the table, waving it*

Do you know what the copyist told me when I arrived this morning? That YOU dismissed him for THREE DAYS last week because you said his services weren't needed! THREE DAYS we could have used to prepare those violin parts! 

And the singers—the prima donna herself told me she hasn't seen you at a single rehearsal this week! Where WERE you, Antonio? What could possibly have been more important than the work you promised—PROMISED—to oversee?

*breathing heavily, barely controlling anger*

Ten days, Salieri. We have ten days to salvage this catastrophe before the Emperor and half the nobility of Vienna sit in judgment of our work!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My esteemed colleague, your frustrations are indeed warranted, and I humbly accept the weight of responsibility for the shortcomings in my absence. It is clear that my actions have not lived up to the standards of organization and discipline that are expected of me, and for this, I offer my sincerest apologies.

I acknowledge that the trust you placed in me was not upheld to the degree it should have been. The incident with the copyist was a grave error on my part, and I deeply regret the impact it had on our preparations. As for my absence from rehearsals, I must confess that I allowed other matters to distract me from my duties, and for that, I am truly sorry.

The task of overseeing the rehearsals and preparations for our opera was indeed entrusted to me, and I failed in that duty. There is no excuse for my lapses, and I understand the gravity of the situation we now find ourselves in with only ten days remaining until the premiere.

I am fully committed to making amends and working tirelessly alongside you to rectify these issues. Together, we must focus our efforts on ensuring that our production meets the standards expected by the Emperor and the Viennese nobility. I will redouble my dedication to the task at hand and do everything in my power to salvage our opera from this crisis. Your guidance and collaboration will be invaluable in these trying times, and I am ready to heed your direction to bring our work back on track.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at him incredulously, then lets out a harsh, bitter laugh*

"Other matters distracted you"? OTHER MATTERS? What other matters, Antonio? What could possibly—

*stops abruptly, eyes narrowing with sudden suspicion*

Wait. Wait just a moment. The copyist said something else... something about you spending hours closeted away in the music library. And Müller, the violinist, he mentioned seeing you at the Burgtheater twice last week—at performances you had no business attending when you should have been HERE!

*steps closer, voice dropping but losing none of its intensity*

There are rumors, Salieri. Whispers in the coffee houses. About that young prodigy—Mozart. They say he's been making quite the stir lately, that new concert of his at the Trattnerhof... 

*eyes flash with sudden understanding and renewed anger*

Is THAT where you were? Chasing after that insufferable boy's performances while MY opera—OUR work—crumbled to pieces? Were you so busy obsessing over Mozart's latest trivial entertainment that you couldn't be bothered to fulfill your obligations to me?

*voice rising again*

Tell me the truth, Antonio! I deserve that much at least! Where were you really, and why did you abandon your duties?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*pauses for a moment, visibly taken aback by the accusations, before regaining composure*

Herr Composer, I must address these rumors directly. It is true that I have attended performances by young Mozart, as I have a keen interest in the musical developments of our time. However, I assure you that my visits to the music library and the Burgtheater were not at the expense of our opera preparations.

I may have allowed myself to become engrossed in Mozart's talents, for he is indeed a remarkable young composer, but I never neglected our work intentionally. If my actions have led to such a perception, I deeply regret any harm caused to our collaboration.

I take full responsibility for any lapses in judgment that may have occurred, and I understand your disappointment in me. Please believe that I am fully committed to salvaging our opera in the time we have left. I will redouble my efforts and focus solely on our work to ensure that we deliver a performance worthy of our talents and the Emperor's patronage.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face turns red with fury, voice shaking*

NOT at the expense of our preparations? NOT AT THE EXPENSE? The second violin parts are MISSING, Salieri! The singers are unprepared! My stage directions have been ALTERED without permission! And you stand there telling me you never neglected our work INTENTIONALLY?

*slams fist on the table*

What difference does intention make when the result is the same catastrophic failure? You think the Emperor will care about your INTENTIONS when the curtain rises on chaos? You think the critics will write "Well, the opera was a disaster, but at least Maestro Salieri's heart was in the right place"?

*voice dripping with scorn*

"A remarkable young composer"—Mozart! That preening peacock who can barely conduct himself with propriety in polite society! THAT is what captured your attention while our deadline approached? While I was away serving the Emperor's interests, you were mooning over Mozart like some starstruck apprentice!

*paces furiously*

And you STILL haven't answered my question directly! Were you at Mozart's performances when you should have been at our rehearsals? Yes or no, Antonio! Stop hiding behind these diplomatic phrases and tell me the TRUTH! Did you or did you not attend Mozart's concerts instead of overseeing the work you promised to manage?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My dear colleague, I must face your accusations with a heavy heart and a clear conscience. I cannot deny the truth of your words, for I must take responsibility for my actions and their consequences. It is apparent that my priorities were misplaced, and I allowed myself to be swayed by external distractions at the expense of our shared work on the Imperial opera.

I must confess that yes, I did attend Mozart's performances during the time when I should have been fully focused on our rehearsals and preparations. My fascination with Mozart's talent and burgeoning reputation led me astray from my duties, and for that, I am deeply remorseful. I understand the gravity of my actions and the impact they have had on our collaboration, and I can offer no excuse for my behavior.

Your anger and disappointment are entirely justified, and I accept them with humility and contrition. I failed in my obligations to you, our work, and the Emperor, and for that, I am truly sorry. I understand that my words may offer little solace in the face of the challenges we now face, but I pledge to you my unwavering commitment to rectifying the situation to the best of my abilities.

I ask for your forgiveness and understanding as we navigate these difficult circumstances together. Let us set aside past grievances and focus on salvaging our opera in the time we have left before the premiere. With your guidance and cooperation, I am determined to make amends and ensure that our performance meets the standards of excellence that our artistry demands.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at him for a long moment, jaw clenched, then speaks in a low, dangerous voice*

Forgiveness? You want my FORGIVENESS? Antonio, you have jeopardized not only this production, but MY reputation! MY standing at court! Do you think the Emperor will distinguish between your failures and mine when this opera falls apart? Do you think he'll say, "Well, it was Salieri's fault, not the other composer's"?

*voice cracking with a mixture of rage and desperation*

No! We will BOTH be disgraced! And for what? So you could sit in the gallery watching that insufferable child prance about the keyboard? Mozart has everything handed to him—natural talent that requires no effort, no discipline, no WORK—and you abandoned our partnership to worship at his altar!

*runs hand through hair, trying to control emotions*

Ten days, Salieri. Ten days to teach singers their parts, copy missing orchestral music, restore my stage directions, and somehow coordinate this shambles into a coherent performance. And you stand there asking for my "guidance and cooperation" as if we're equals in this disaster!

*points finger accusingly*

Here is what WILL happen: You will personally supervise every remaining rehearsal. You will sit with the copyist until EVERY missing part is written out, even if it takes all night. You will apologize to the prima donna and beg her to work with you. And you will NOT—do you hear me?—you will NOT set foot in any theater, concert hall, or anywhere near Mozart until after our premiere!

Do I make myself clear?

transcript.text:

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*lets out an exasperated breath, shaking head*

Your compliance means NOTHING to me right now, Antonio. Only results. I don't want your gratitude or your promises—I've already seen what those are worth.

*begins gathering papers from the table, movements sharp and agitated*

We start immediately. The singers are scheduled for rehearsal in one hour. You WILL be there, and you will work with them until they know every entrance, every cue. I don't care if it takes until midnight.

*turns back to face him, voice still tight with anger*

And another thing—those stage directions that were changed. Who authorized that? Was that you as well, or did you allow someone else to meddle in my work while you were off indulging your Mozart obsession? Because I want NAMES, Salieri. If someone else interfered, they will answer for it too.

*picks up the portfolio, clutching it tightly*

I'm going now to meet with the copyist myself—clearly I cannot trust this to anyone else. When I return in two hours, I expect to find you at the rehearsal, WORKING. Not making excuses, not offering apologies, but actually DOING what you should have been doing all along.

*pauses at the doorway, looking back with barely contained fury*

And Salieri? If you fail me again—if there is even ONE more lapse—I will take this directly to the Emperor myself. Your career at this court will be FINISHED. Do you understand me?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stops in the doorway, shoulders tense, then turns back one more time with cold fury*

You were "not aware" of changes to MY stage directions? In a production YOU were managing? That is perhaps even WORSE than if you had made them yourself! It shows you weren't even PAYING ATTENTION to what was happening!

*voice rises again despite obvious effort to control it*

Do you understand what you're admitting? That you were so distracted, so utterly consumed with Mozart and whatever else occupied your time, that you didn't even NOTICE when someone tampered with my work? Someone walked into OUR rehearsals, changed MY artistic decisions, and you—the man I entrusted with EVERYTHING—you didn't even KNOW?

*takes a step back into the room*

This is beyond incompetence, Antonio. This is complete abandonment of duty. And you stand there thanking me for "holding you accountable" as if this were some minor correction between colleagues!

*voice drops to an icy whisper*

One hour. The singers. And you had better pray to God that you can undo some of this damage, because I am THIS close to going to the Emperor right now and withdrawing from this entire collaboration. The only reason I haven't is because it would ruin us BOTH—but at this point, I'm starting to think my reputation might survive better with an honest withdrawal than with this impending catastrophe.

Now GET OUT of my sight and go prepare for that rehearsal!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face contorted with rage and disbelief*

STOP! Just STOP with these endless apologies and assurances! Every word out of your mouth is "I understand," "I will," "I appreciate"—ENOUGH! I don't want to hear another word of your contrition! I want ACTION!

*voice breaking slightly with the strain*

Do you think I ENJOY this? Do you think I take pleasure in berating a colleague I once considered a friend? I trusted you, Antonio! I defended you when others at court whispered that you were too consumed with envy of younger talents! I told them they were wrong, that you were a dedicated professional!

*laughs bitterly*

And now I discover they were RIGHT! You WERE obsessed with Mozart! So obsessed that you destroyed everything we worked for!

*moves toward the door again, voice exhausted but still angry*

Get out of here. Go to the rehearsal hall. I can't bear to look at you right now. When I return in two hours, you had BETTER have made progress with those singers, or I swear to you, Antonio, this partnership is OVER, and I will make certain everyone at court knows exactly why.

*pauses, then adds with bitter finality*

One more thing—stay away from me until the premiere is done. Work through my assistant if you need to communicate. I don't trust myself to speak civilly to you again.

Now GO!

transcript.text:
*throws hands up in complete exasperation*

MOTHER OF GOD, SALIERI! Are you INCAPABLE of simply leaving without another speech? I said GO! That means LEAVE! DEPART! REMOVE YOURSELF FROM MY PRESENCE!

*voice reaching a breaking point*

You're STILL standing here talking! "Thank you for your candor," "I will not let you down"—these are MORE empty words! Do you not comprehend the meaning of SILENCE? Of ACTION INSTEAD OF WORDS?

*practically shouting now*

Every SECOND you waste standing here spouting these platitudes is another second NOT spent with those singers! It's been nearly TEN MINUTES since I first told you to go, and you're STILL HERE, still talking, still "acknowledging" and "respecting my request"!

*gestures frantically toward the door*

The rehearsal hall is THAT WAY! The singers are waiting! The clock is ticking! And yet here you stand, PARALYZING yourself with more apologies and assurances! Is this what you did for the past two weeks? Stand around TALKING about work instead of DOING it?

*voice hoarse with fury and frustration*

GET. OUT. NOW! Not another word! Not one more syllable! MOVE!

YOU'RE STILL TALKING! STILL! APOLOGIZING! AGAIN!

*breathing heavily, barely able to speak*

LEAVE! NOW! WITHOUT! ANOTHER! WORD!

*turns away, unable to even look at him anymore*
